summary: Admission controller annotation enforcement causes runner pods to be rejected during credential rotation
description: Issue summary: During the scheduled Vault transit key rotation on 2026-03-12 at 03:00 UTC, the cluster admission controller started rejecting self-hosted runner pods that did not include the new required annotation (assembly.redwood.com/cred-rotation=2026-03-12). Impact: ~120 queued release jobs across two orgs failed to provision runners and remained in Pending state for ~45 minutes. Affected services: CI/CD canary and nightly release pipelines; customer-facing builds were delayed. Steps to reproduce: 1) Trigger a runner pod create without the annotation (kubectl apply -f runner-pod.yaml). 2) Observe admission controller deny event. 3) Check runner-manager logs for provisioning backoff. Observed behavior: admission controller returns 403 with message "missing required cred-rotation annotation" for pods created by runner-manager. Expected behavior: runner-manager should either be updated to attach the annotation or admission policy should permit existing pods during rotation. Relevant logs/dashboards: - Kibana: logs/dashboard link: https://kibana.redwood.local/app/logs#/discover?_a=(query:...) - PagerDuty incident: PD-78321 - Affected node pools: ci-workers-*-uswest (spot-backed), which experienced high churn during restart window.
comments: 2026-03-12 03:28 - Leah Martinez: Initial triage - noticed admission denies after Vault rewrap job completed. Runners created by runner-manager v1.14.2 are missing new annotation. Queue depth spiking in ci-orchestrator.

2026-03-12 03:42 - Samir Patel: Repro'd in staging by applying a manifest without annotation. Admission webhook config shows required_annotations enforcement introduced by infra PR #1289 (kube-policy). Rolling back webhook admission rule to previous version reduced rejections. Preparing a targeted rollback in prod.

2026-03-12 04:05 - Anya Chen (SRE): Temporarily disabled annotation enforcement in us-west to allow in-flight runner provisioning. Noted increased risk window; notified Release Eng and Security. Opened follow-up to harden vault-sync to add annotation upstream.

2026-03-12 10:15 - Release Eng (Tom Nguyen): Patch for runner-manager to emit assembly.redwood.com/cred-rotation annotation prepared in infra repo. Will ship as hotfix 1.14.3. Validated pod create with new image in staging.

2026-03-13 01:07 - Samir Patel: Hotfix 1.14.3 rolled across ci-runner fleets; observed normal provisioning and drain of backlog. Re-enabled annotation enforcement in admission controller and validated acceptance of new pods.
2026-03-14 09:30 - Leah Martinez: Post-incident review scheduled; recommended runbook updates and a temporary flag for admission policies during credential rotations.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: admission policy was tightened in infra PR 1289 but runner-manager was not synchronized with new annotation requirement before vault rewrap completed.
kubectl get events --field-selector reason=FailedAdmissionWebhook -n ci-prod -> many entries 'missing required cred-rotation annotation'
AdmissionWebhook configuration snapshot: kubectl get ValidatingWebhookConfiguration kube-policy -o yaml (see related_confluence_pages for snapshot).
Runner-manager image: registry.redwood/cirunner:1.14.2 (does not include annotation injection code path). Hotfix builds add metadata in pod template generation.
Observed token lifecycle: Vault rewrap short TTL (3600s) caused quick rotation; onboarding window for runner-manager update missed due to deployment rollout cadence.
CI queue depth: max 124 pending runner requests at 03:18 UTC; mean pod create latency increased 3x.
Manual mitigation steps tested: - disable admission enforcement; - deploy runner-manager 1.14.3 with annotation; - re-enable enforcement; all validated in canary us-west-1a before full enable.
Related traces: trace ids trace-prod-ccf9 and trace-prod-d1b8 correlate with runner-manager create requests.
Related existing tickets reviewed: INT-620743 (proxy tls rotation), INT-35720 (agent bootstrap token expiry)
resolution: Root cause: timing mismatch between cluster admission policy rollout (requiring assembly.redwood.com/cred-rotation annotation) and runner-manager rollout; Vault rewrap completed triggering enforcement earlier than runner-manager update. Fix applied: 1) Deployed runner-manager hotfix v1.14.3 to emit required annotation. 2) Temporarily disabled annotation enforcement during immediate recovery window, then re-enabled after validation. 3) Updated deployment pipeline to include annotation compatibility gate before admission policy changes are promoted. 4) Increased Vault rewrap notification to downstream services and added a 30-minute grace window for admission policy activation during credential rotations. Follow-ups: - Create automated pre-flight check in infra CI to validate that all runner-producing services include required annotations before merging admission policy PRs. - Update runbook: CONFLUENCE-Runbooks/Credential-Rotation to include a rollback playbook and communications checklist. - Schedule cross-team drill for secret rotations. Incident closed after backlog drained and normal provisioning observed for 24h.
